procedure.description: bilateral upper eyelid blepharoplasty with excessive skin weighting down the lid

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Prairie Commons Medicaid Plan denied the claim for CPT 15823 (bilateral upper eyelid blepharoplasty with excessive skin weighting down the lid) with date of service 2026-06-24. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Visual field documentation submitted does not meet the policy threshold for functional impairment.

criteria.text: Automated visual field testing demonstrating at least 30 percent loss of the superior visual field, with improvement when the upper lids are taped.
Photographs documenting redundant upper lid skin resting on or over the lashes, or a margin reflex distance 1 of 2 millimeters or less.
A documented functional complaint such as difficulty reading or driving, loss of the superior field, or brow fatigue.

chart.text: Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

60 year old woman sent over by her eye doctor for heavy upper lids. Exam: marked dermatochalasis both upper lids, skin hooding over the lashes laterally, brow ptosis mild, no true ptosis of the lid itself, levator function good. Discussed upper lid blepharoplasty. Her history otherwise: hypertension on lisinopril. Surgeries: wisdom teeth. Allergies: no drug allergies. Does not smoke, a glass of wine on weekends, works as a nurse. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. She says she is lifting her brows all day to see, gets a headache by evening, has given up night driving, tilts her head back to read the paper.
Humphrey superior field, untaped: 9 degrees of superior field loss on the right and 8 on the left, roughly 16 percent. Taped: modest improvement, about 3 degrees each side.
Gastroenterology note received. Screening colonoscopy completed, two small polyps removed, benign on pathology, repeat in 5 years.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 1.3, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 75. Repeat in a year.
Back to review the testing. Went over the operation, bruising, the scar in the crease, the small chance of dry eye. She wants to go ahead. Vitals today 126 over 71, pulse 65.
Frontal and lateral photos today, primary gaze, flash. Redundant upper lid skin draping onto the lashes on both sides. MRD1 about 2 millimeters right and 2 left.
Patient called about a tick bite on the calf after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.

Here with a cough and congestion for 9 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if she gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.

Mole on the right calf that her spouse noticed. About 4 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change she is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.
Nurse call. Patient had questions about time off work after surgery and whether she needs someone at home the first night. Answered both, she will arrange it.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 19 and 13. No ocular pathology noted.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the fall. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Letter from the dentist's office confirming routine cleaning and exam completed, no active infection, no dental work pending. Sent at our request for the surgical file.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the right for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
Work note requested for a sick day last Monday. Faxed to the employer.
Mammogram report forwarded for the record. Bilateral screening, BI-RADS 1, negative, routine screening in one year.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Blood pressure check. 123 over 84 today, 121 over 77 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 40 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.
Pre-op. Consent signed. Marked the skin excision sitting up. No blood thinners. Stop the fish oil.

Annual physical. Feels well overall. Sleeping fine, appetite fine, no chest pain, no shortness of breath. Flu shot given in the left arm today. Due for a tetanus booster, she will think about it. Labs ordered, fasting.

expected.note: The chart raises crit-1 (vft) but does not satisfy it; the mention is a plan or a shortfall, not completed treatment or a met threshold.
